controls.label: memory_limit=-1, set where applications cannot override it
controls.what: memory_limit=-1, set where applications cannot override it (php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache config); check no pool, directory or app setting restores a finite limit.
controls.caveat: Removes the controllable memory-limit failure; an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path.

controls.label: Low post_max_size and upload limits, and request-size limits at the web server or proxy
controls.what: A low post_max_size (8M without uploads, 32M with), upload_max_filesize below it, and web-server or proxy limits on decoded request size, field count, multipart part count, header count and nesting depth, including for requests without a usable Content-Length.
controls.caveat: Reduces exposure to specific attack paths; does not make an installation safe.

controls.label: A container or cgroup memory limit as an availability boundary
controls.what: A container or cgroup memory limit as an availability boundary, killing only the affected worker.
controls.caveat: Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA: they can cause the vulnerable allocation failure.

controls.label: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini or the pool, workers restarted
controls.what: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini, the FPM pool or server configuration, then restart every worker.
controls.caveat: Blocks the confirmed session paths only. ini_set() and .user.ini are too late.

controls.label: fatal_error_backtraces=0 (PHP 8.5), workers restarted
controls.caveat: Blocks the confirmed fatal-backtrace path only.

controls.label: Invalid per-request settings and reachable fatal errors removed
controls.what: Remove invalid or deprecated per-request settings that emit diagnostics before initialisation; fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts.
controls.caveat: Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting, display_errors or @ does not help.

vulns.impact: remote code execution as the PHP worker, across requests on the same worker (mod_php and FPM, demonstrated)
